AK.name: Alaska

pollHours.note: Local time. Most of Alaska uses Alaska Time; the western Aleutian Islands use Hawaii-Aleutian Time.

earlyVoting.note: Early and in-person absentee voting run from Oct 19 through Election Day (Nov 3). Each location sets its own hours.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by Oct 24, 2026 (online-delivery ballot requests by Nov 2)
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Postmarked by Nov 3, received by Nov 13, 2026 (Nov 18 if mailed from overseas); hand-delivered ballots must reach a voting location by 8:00 PM Nov 3
mailBallot.note: Sign the return envelope in front of a witness who is 18 or older, and include at least one identifier. Ask the post office to hand-cancel it so the postmark is on time.

AK.sameDayRegistrationNote: Alaska does not offer same-day registration for this election.
AK.registrationNote: The deadline to register or update your registration was Oct 4, 2026. No registration option remains for Nov 3.
AK.voterId: Show one form of ID, such as your voter card, driver's license, state ID, passport, hunting or fishing license, or a current bill, bank statement, paycheck, or government document with your name and address; without ID you can vote a questioned ballot.
AK.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close at 8:00 PM, you can still vote.

AL.name: Alabama

pollHours.note: Local time. Most of Alabama is on Central Time; polling places in the few areas that observe Eastern Time may run 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM Eastern.

earlyVoting.note: Alabama has no early voting open to everyone. Voters with a valid excuse could vote absentee in person at their county Absentee Election Manager's office (usually the Circuit Clerk); in-person applications closed Oct 29, 2026.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by mail by Oct 27, 2026, or delivered in person by Oct 29, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: By mail: received by noon on Election Day, Nov 3, 2026. By hand: delivered by close of business (no later than 5:00 PM) on Nov 2, 2026
mailBallot.note: Valid reasons include being away from your county, illness or disability, and certain work shifts. Include a copy of your photo ID with your application. Emergency absentee applications are allowed until 5:00 PM on Nov 2 for certain last-minute emergencies.

AL.sameDayRegistrationNote: Alabama does not offer Election Day registration.
AL.registrationNote: The registration deadline was Oct 19, 2026 (online by 11:59 PM). It is too late to register for this election.
AL.voterId: Bring a valid photo ID such as an Alabama driver's license or non-driver ID (expired less than 60 days is OK), free Alabama Photo Voter ID, U.S. passport, military ID, tribal ID, or a government, college, or university ID; without one you can vote only if two poll workers positively identify you, or else by provisional ballot.
AL.lineRule: If you are in line by 7:00 PM, you can still vote. No one may join the line after 7:00 PM.

AR.name: Arkansas

earlyVoting.note: Weekdays 8 AM to 6 PM and Saturdays 10 AM to 4 PM; no Sundays. Early voting ends at 5 PM on Monday, Nov 2. Off-site locations and hours vary by county; check your county clerk.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by Oct 27, 2026 (by mail, fax, or email); in person by close of business Oct 30, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by 7:30 PM on Election Day (by mail)
mailBallot.note: You qualify if you will be away on Election Day, are ill or disabled, or are military/overseas. If you hand-deliver your ballot, the county clerk must receive it by close of business Friday, Oct 30. Include a copy of your photo ID.

AR.sameDayRegistrationNote: Arkansas does not offer same-day registration. Registered voters who moved to a new county can update their registration, including on Election Day.
AR.registrationNote: The deadline was Oct 5, 2026. There is no way left to register for the Nov 3 election.
AR.voterId: Bring photo ID, such as an Arkansas driver's license or state ID, U.S. passport, military ID, Arkansas college ID, concealed carry license, public assistance ID, or a free voter verification card from your county clerk; without it you vote a provisional ballot that counts only if you show ID to the county clerk or election commission by noon Monday, Nov 9.
AR.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close, you can still vote.
AR.sourceNote: The list of accepted photo IDs and the Monday-noon cure deadline come from the University of Arkansas Extension 2026 voter handout, not the Secretary of State site. The in-line-at-closing rule was not confirmed on an official page.

AZ.name: Arizona

earlyVoting.note: In-person early voting ended at 7:00 PM Friday, Oct 30. Locations vary by county; check your county. From then until 5:00 PM Monday, Nov 2, you can vote early only if you sign a statement that an emergency keeps you from voting on Election Day.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by 5:00 PM on Oct 23, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by 7:00 PM on Election Day
mailBallot.note: Postmarks do not count; officials suggested mailing by Oct 27. Now, drop your signed ballot at any drop box, early voting site, or polling place/vote center in your county by 7 PM Nov 3.

AZ.sameDayRegistrationNote: Arizona does not offer Election Day registration.
AZ.registrationNote: The deadline was Oct 5, 2026 (11:59 PM). If you are not registered, you cannot vote in this election.
AZ.voterId: Bring one ID showing your name and current address (Arizona driver's license, Arizona ID, tribal ID, or other government ID), or two documents with your name and address such as a utility bill and bank statement; without proper ID you can vote a provisional or conditional provisional ballot.
AZ.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close at 7 PM, you can still vote.
AZ.sourceNote: azsos.gov (Secretary of State) and Maricopa County election pages returned 403 to every fetch. Dates and hours come from the Citizens Clean Elections Commission (a state agency, azcleanelections.gov) and the Arizona Revised Statutes on azleg.gov.

CA.name: California

earlyVoting.note: Early voting sites could open Oct 5; in Voter's Choice Act counties, vote centers open by Oct 24. Varies by county; check your county.

mailBallot.returnDeadline: Postmarked on or before Nov 3, received by Nov 10, 2026
mailBallot.note: Every active registered voter is mailed a ballot. You can also return it at a drop box, vote center, or any polling place in your county by 8:00 PM on Election Day.

CA.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can still register and vote (conditional, or Same Day, voter registration) at your county elections office, a vote center, or a polling place through Election Day. Your ballot is counted once your registration is verified.
CA.registrationNote: The regular deadline was Oct 19, 2026. From Oct 20 through Nov 3, you can still register and vote in person with Same Day (conditional) registration.
CA.voterId: Most voters do not need to show ID; if you are voting for the first time and registered by mail without a driver's license or Social Security number, bring ID or a document with your name and address.
CA.lineRule: If you are in line at 8:00 PM when polls close, you can still vote.
CA.sourceNote: The 8:00 PM line rule comes from the Secretary of State's June 2, 2026 primary voter-tips release, not a general-election page. The rule is set by statute.

CO.name: Colorado

earlyVoting.note: Vote in person at any Voter Service and Polling Center in your county. Centers open by Oct 19 and stay open through Election Day, except Sundays and the first Saturday of the period. Locations and hours vary by county; check GoVoteColorado.gov.

mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by your county clerk by 7:00 PM on Election Day, Nov 3, 2026
mailBallot.note: Every active voter is mailed a ballot. Postmarks do not count, so this close to Election Day use a drop box or drop-off location. If there is a signature or ID problem, you have until 11:59 PM on Nov 11, 2026 to fix it.

CO.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can register and vote in person at a Voter Service and Polling Center in your county through 7:00 PM on Election Day. Bring an acceptable ID.
CO.registrationNote: The deadline to register and still get a ballot by mail was Oct 26, 2026. You can still register and vote in person at a Voter Service and Polling Center through Election Day.
CO.voterId: Bring a Colorado driver's license or state ID, U.S. passport, military ID, or another listed ID; a utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, or government document from the last 60 days with your name and a Colorado address also works.
CO.lineRule: If you are in line by 7:00 PM, you can still vote.

CT.name: Connecticut

earlyVoting.note: Every day, usually 10 AM to 6 PM; open 8 AM to 8 PM on Oct 27 and Oct 29. No early voting on Nov 2. Each town has its own early voting site, which may differ from your Election Day polling place.

mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by 8:00 PM on Election Day
mailBallot.note: Return by mail, at your town's secure drop box, or in person to your Town Clerk. You can fix (cure) a problem with your ballot until 8:00 PM on Election Day.

CT.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can register and vote on Election Day at your town's designated Same-Day Registration site (not your regular polling place). Bring proof of identity and proof of residence. You must be in line by 8:00 PM.
CT.registrationNote: The regular registration deadline was Oct 16, 2026. You can still register and vote on Nov 3 at your town's Same-Day Registration site.
CT.voterId: Poll workers will ask for ID, but photo ID is not required; a Social Security card or any pre-printed ID showing your name and address, signature, or photo works, and if you have no ID you can usually sign an affidavit instead (some first-time voters who registered by mail must show ID or a document with their address, or vote provisionally).
CT.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close at 8:00 PM, you can still vote.
CT.sourceNote: The general line rule at regular polling places is confirmed on the official page only for Same-Day Registration sites (in line by 8:00 PM).

DC.name: District of Columbia

pollHours.note: You can vote at any Vote Center in DC on Election Day.

earlyVoting.note: Early Vote Centers are open every day, 8:30 AM to 7:00 PM. You can register and vote at the same time.

mailBallot.returnDeadline: Postmarked by Nov 3, received by Nov 13, 2026; or put in a drop box or at a Vote Center by 8:00 PM on Nov 3
mailBallot.note: Ballots are mailed to all registered voters. Drop boxes are open through 8:00 PM on Nov 3. The deadline to fix (cure) a mail ballot problem is Nov 19.

DC.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can register and vote at any Vote Center on Election Day. Bring proof of residence with your name and current DC address, such as a DC ID, a recent utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, government document, or lease.
DC.registrationNote: The deadline for online and mail registration was Oct 13, 2026. You can still register and vote at a Vote Center on Election Day, Nov 3.
DC.voterId: Most voters do not need ID; if you are registering at a Vote Center, or are a first-time voter whose identity was not verified when you registered, bring proof of residence such as a DC ID, utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, government document, or lease.
DC.lineRule: If you are in line at 8:00 PM, you can still vote.
DC.sourceNote: The first-time-voter ID rule is the federal HAVA rule; no DCBOE page I read stated it directly.

DE.name: Delaware

earlyVoting.note: Vote at any early voting site in your county. No early voting on Sunday, Oct 25. Hours were 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM Oct 22-27 and 11:00 AM to 7:00 PM Oct 28-Nov 1.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Absentee ballots can be issued by your county Department of Elections office until noon on Nov 2, 2026 (the last day to mail them was Oct 30)
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by your county Department of Elections office by 8:00 PM on Election Day (Nov 3, 2026)
mailBallot.note: Allowed reasons include work, illness or disability, caregiving, military or public service, and being away. Return by mail or by hand to your county office; ballots are not accepted at early voting sites or polling places.

DE.sameDayRegistrationNote: Delaware does not offer same-day registration.
DE.registrationNote: The deadline was 11:59 PM on Oct 10, 2026 (Oct 19 for military and overseas voters). No registration option remains for Nov 3.
DE.voterId: Show proof of identity (a photo is not required); if you do not have it, you can sign an affidavit that you are the registered voter and still vote.
DE.lineRule: If you are in line at 8:00 PM, you can still vote.

FL.name: Florida

pollHours.note: Local time. Most of Florida is on Eastern time; much of the Panhandle west of the Apalachicola River is on Central time.

earlyVoting.note: Every county must hold early voting Oct 24-31. Counties could add days as early as Oct 19 and as late as Nov 1. Varies by county; check your county.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Request by 5:00 PM on Oct 22, 2026 for a ballot to be mailed; you can still pick up your own ballot at your Supervisor of Elections office through Election Day (an emergency affidavit is required from Oct 24 on)
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by 7:00 PM local time on Election Day (postmarks do not count)
mailBallot.note: You can drop off your ballot at your Supervisor of Elections office drop boxes until 7:00 PM on Election Day, or at early voting site drop boxes during early voting. If your signature is missing or does not match, you have until 5:00 PM on Nov 5 to fix it.

FL.sameDayRegistrationNote: Florida does not have same-day registration.
FL.registrationNote: The deadline was Oct 5, 2026. There is no way left to register for the Nov 3 election.
FL.voterId: Bring a current, valid photo ID with your signature, such as a Florida driver's license or ID card, U.S. passport, debit or credit card, military, student, or government employee ID; if the photo ID has no signature, bring a second ID that does; without ID you can vote a provisional ballot.
FL.lineRule: If you are in line at 7:00 PM when polls close, you can still vote.
FL.sourceNote: WebFetch got 403 on www.dos.fl.gov, so we read the official pages with curl instead. The optional early-voting dates (Oct 19 and Nov 1) are our math from the statewide rule on the page (15th to 2nd day before the election). The time-zone note comes from general knowledge.

GA.name: Georgia

earlyVoting.note: Ends Friday, Oct 30. Sites, hours, and weekend days vary by county; check your county.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by your county by Oct 23, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by 7:00 PM on Election Day
mailBallot.note: Drop boxes are only inside early voting sites during early voting hours (ending Oct 30). After that, mail it or deliver it to your county registrar's office by 7:00 PM on Nov 3.

GA.sameDayRegistrationNote: Georgia does not offer same-day registration.
GA.registrationNote: The deadline was Oct 5, 2026. Registration is closed for this election.
GA.voterId: Bring a physical photo ID such as a Georgia driver's license (even if expired), a state or federal ID card, a free Georgia voter ID card, a U.S. passport, a government employee photo ID, a military ID, or a tribal photo ID; without one you can vote a provisional ballot and must show ID to your county registrar within three days.
GA.lineRule: If you are in line by 7:00 PM, you can still vote.
GA.sourceNote: The Secretary of State site (sos.ga.gov) blocked all fetches (403). Dates, hours, mail rules and the in-line rule come from the official state portal georgia.gov. The list of accepted IDs comes from NCSL (Ga. Code 21-2-417); NCSL also notes a 2025 law (HB 296) requiring the ID to be a physical card, not a digital ID.

HI.name: Hawaii

pollHours.note: Hawaii votes by mail. These are Election Day hours for in-person voter service centers. Mail ballots and drop box ballots must arrive by 7:00 PM.

earlyVoting.note: In-person voting at voter service centers, Monday through Saturday (no Sundays), usually 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM. A few sites on Maui and Oahu have shorter schedules; check your county.

mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by 7:00 PM on Election Day (Nov 3, 2026); postmarks do not count
mailBallot.note: Ballots were mailed around Oct 16. Drop boxes (places of deposit) are open through 7:00 PM on Nov 3. Sign the return envelope or your ballot will not count.

HI.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can register and vote in person at any voter service center in your county through 7:00 PM on Election Day.
HI.registrationNote: The paper application deadline was Oct 26, 2026. You can still register and vote in person at a voter service center through Nov 3. Online registration (needs a Hawaii driver license or state ID) is also listed as available at any time.
HI.voterId: Most voters do not need ID; if you are a first-time Hawaii voter who registered by mail without a Hawaii license, state ID, or Social Security number, bring a photo ID or a current bill, bank statement, paycheck, or government document with your name and address.
HI.lineRule: If you are in line at a voter service center by 7:00 PM, you can still vote.
HI.sourceNote: The ID rule for first-time mail registrants comes from Office of Elections registration guidance (search excerpt) and NCSL; no official page fetched stated in-person ID rules directly. The 7:00 PM line rule is from the Office of Elections 2026 primary news release.

IA.name: Iowa

earlyVoting.note: In-person absentee voting at your county auditor's office, weekdays during office hours, ending 5:00 PM Nov 2. Some auditors are also open Saturday, Oct 31; check your county.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by 5:00 PM on Oct 19, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by 8:00 PM on Election Day
mailBallot.note: A postmark is not enough; the county auditor must have your ballot by 8:00 PM Nov 3. You can return it in person to the auditor's office.

IA.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can register and vote on Election Day at the polling place for your current address. Bring proof of identity and proof of residence (an Iowa driver's license with your current address covers both), or have a registered voter from your precinct attest for you.
IA.registrationNote: The pre-registration deadline was Oct 19, 2026. You can still register and vote at your polling place on Election Day.
IA.voterId: Bring an Iowa driver's license or non-operator ID, U.S. passport, military or veteran ID, tribal ID, or your signed Iowa Voter ID PIN card; without one you can vote a provisional ballot and show ID later.
IA.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close, you can still vote.
IA.sourceNote: sos.iowa.gov returned 403 to both WebFetch and curl, so facts come from official county auditor sites (Marion, Jasper), which apply state law. The in-line-at-closing rule was not confirmed on an official page.

ID.name: Idaho

pollHours.note: Polls are open 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM local time; some county clerks open at 7:00 AM. Northern Idaho is on Pacific Time and the rest of the state on Mountain Time.

earlyVoting.note: Varies by county; check your county. Counties could start as early as Oct 13 (for example, Ada and Bonner started Oct 19), and early voting ended at 5:00 PM on Friday, Oct 30. A few counties offer in-person absentee voting instead.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by 5:00 PM on Oct 23, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by 8:00 PM on Election Day
mailBallot.note: Your county clerk must have the ballot by 8:00 PM Nov 3; a postmark is not enough.

ID.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can register and vote at your polling place on Election Day. Bring a photo ID and proof of residence, such as a utility bill (not a cell phone bill), lease, bank statement, or paystub.
ID.registrationNote: The pre-registration deadline was Oct 23, 2026 (5 PM for paper forms; online registration also closed Oct 23). You can still register and vote at your polling place on Election Day.
ID.voterId: Bring an Idaho driver's license or ID card, U.S. passport or federal photo ID, tribal ID, or Idaho concealed weapons license; if you don't have one, you can sign a Personal Identification Affidavit and vote a regular ballot.
ID.lineRule: If you are in line by 8:00 PM on Election Day, you can still vote.
ID.sourceNote: The statewide early voting window (earliest start Oct 13, end 5 PM Oct 30) comes from Idaho Capital Sun / States Newsroom reporting of a Secretary of State list (pages blocked; read via search snippets); Bonner County's official notice confirms Oct 19-30 there. The absentee request and registration deadline (Oct 23) come from Bonner County's official notice. The 7:00 AM option comes from NCSL (Idaho Code 34-1101).

IL.name: Illinois

pollHours.note: Central Time statewide.

earlyVoting.note: Starts Sept 24 at election authority offices; other permanent sites open by Oct 19 and must be open weekends. Varies by county; check your county.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by mail by Oct 29, 2026; in person at your election office by Nov 2, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Postmarked by Nov 3, received by Nov 17, 2026
mailBallot.note: You can also return it to a county drop box or your election office by 7:00 PM on Election Day. Some drop boxes close earlier.

IL.sameDayRegistrationNote: Grace period registration lets you register and vote at the same time through Election Day. Bring two IDs, one showing your current address. On Election Day, it is offered at your election office and, in many counties, at your home precinct polling place; check your county.
IL.registrationNote: Regular registration closed Oct 6, 2026, and online registration closed Oct 18, 2026. You can still register and vote in person through Nov 3 with grace period registration.
IL.voterId: Most registered voters do not need to show ID; bring two IDs (one with your current address) if you are registering on the spot, and some first-time voters who registered by mail may be asked for ID.
IL.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close, you can still vote.
IL.sourceNote: The State Board's calendar page returned errors for date searches, so the full 2026 calendar was read from the Board-issued PDF (amended July 9, 2025) hosted by Effingham County, cross-checked with the DeKalb County clerk and the Board's live calendar list. The in-line rule is from an Illinois Attorney General notice citing 10 ILCS 5/17-1. The polling-place ID details for grace period registration come from news coverage (NBC Chicago) and NCSL; the Chicago election board site blocked fetches. The U.S. Supreme Court's June 2026 Watson v. RNC ruling left post-Election Day receipt of postmarked ballots in place.

IN.name: Indiana

pollHours.note: Local time. Most counties are on Eastern time; 12 counties in the northwest and southwest corners (such as Lake, Porter, and Vanderburgh) are on Central time, so their polls close an hour later by Eastern clocks.

earlyVoting.note: In-person absentee (early) voting ends at noon local time on Monday, Nov 2. No excuse needed. Sites and hours vary by county; check your county. Counties must be open Saturdays Oct 24 and Oct 31.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by 11:59 PM on Oct 22, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by your county election board by 6:00 PM local time on Election Day
mailBallot.note: You need an approved reason, such as being 65 or older, having a disability, or being away from your county all 12 hours polls are open. Postmarks do not count.

IN.sameDayRegistrationNote: Indiana does not offer Election Day registration.
IN.registrationNote: The deadline was Oct 5, 2026 (close of business in person, midnight online). If you are not registered, you cannot vote in this election.
IN.voterId: Bring a photo ID issued by Indiana or the U.S. government that shows your name and is current or expired after Nov 5, 2024, such as an Indiana driver's license, Indiana ID card, military ID, or U.S. passport; college and school IDs are no longer accepted.
IN.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close at 6 PM, you can still vote.
IN.sourceNote: 2026 dates and poll hours are from the state's 2026 election calendar as republished on Clark County's official in.gov page; the state's 2026 voter guide PDF could not be text-extracted. The line rule (IC 3-11-8-11) was confirmed only from secondary statute summaries and a 2020 public radio report, not an official page. The Central-time county list is from the state's 2024 election results notes.

KS.name: Kansas

pollHours.note: Polls are usually open 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM, but counties may open as early as 6:00 AM and close as late as 8:00 PM (at least 12 hours). Hours are local; a few western counties are on Mountain Time. Check your county.

earlyVoting.note: Varies by county; check your county. Counties could start as early as Oct 14 and had to start by Oct 27. In-person advance voting ends at noon on Monday, Nov 2.

mailBallot.returnDeadline: Postmarked by Nov 3, received by Nov 6, 2026
mailBallot.note: A 2025 law ending the 3-day grace period is blocked by a court order for this election, but the case is still on appeal. To be safe, drop your ballot off at your county election office or a drop box by 7:00 PM Nov 3 instead of mailing it.

KS.sameDayRegistrationNote: Kansas does not offer same-day registration.
KS.registrationNote: The deadline was Oct 13, 2026. There is no way left to register for the Nov 3 election.
KS.voterId: Bring photo ID, such as a driver's license or ID card from any state, U.S. passport, military ID, or certain tribal, government employee, student, concealed carry, or public assistance IDs (voters 65 and older may use an expired ID); without one you vote a provisional ballot that counts only if you show ID before the county canvass.
KS.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close, you can still vote.
KS.sourceNote: The mail-ballot request deadline and the 3-day grace period status come from news reports (KCUR, HPPR), not an official page: an Oct 7, 2026 appeals court ruling kept the grace period in place for November while the challenge to 2025's SB 4 continues. The Nov 2 noon end of advance voting comes from Wyandotte County's official page. The in-line-at-closing rule was not confirmed on an official page.

KY.name: Kentucky

pollHours.note: Local time. Kentucky is split between Eastern and Central time, so polls close an hour later in Central Time counties (by Eastern clock).

earlyVoting.note: No-excuse in-person early voting is Oct 29, 30, and 31 only. Earlier days (Oct 21-23 and Oct 26-28) were only for voters with an approved excuse. Locations and hours are set by each county; check govote.ky.gov or your county clerk.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Requested through the online portal by 11:59 PM Eastern on Oct 20, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by your county clerk by 6:00 PM local time on Election Day, Nov 3, 2026
mailBallot.note: Mail ballots are only for voters with a qualifying reason, such as age, disability, illness, or being temporarily out of state. Every county has a drop box for hand-delivering your ballot.

KY.sameDayRegistrationNote: Kentucky does not offer Election Day registration.
KY.registrationNote: The registration deadline was Oct 5, 2026 (online by 4:00 PM local time, mail postmarked by Oct 5, or in person at the county clerk by close of business).
KY.voterId: Bring a photo ID with your name issued by the U.S. or Kentucky government (such as a driver's license, state ID, or passport), a military ID, a U.S. college or university ID, or a Kentucky city or county government ID.
KY.lineRule: If you are in line at 6:00 PM local time, you can still vote.

LA.name: Louisiana

earlyVoting.note: Early voting was 8:30 AM to 6:00 PM daily, except Sunday, Oct 25, at your parish Registrar of Voters office and other early voting locations. It has ended.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: By 4:30 PM on Oct 30, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by your parish Registrar of Voters by 4:30 PM on Nov 2, 2026 (the day before Election Day)
mailBallot.note: Valid reasons include being 65 or older, having a disability, or being away from your parish during early voting and on Election Day. Return by mail, fax (on request), or hand delivery by you or an immediate family member.

LA.sameDayRegistrationNote: Louisiana does not offer Election Day registration.
LA.registrationNote: The deadline to register in person, by mail, or at an OMV office was Oct 5, 2026. Online registration through GeauxVote closed Oct 13, 2026.
LA.voterId: Bring a Louisiana driver's license, Louisiana special ID card, U.S. military ID with your name and photo, or another photo ID with your name and signature; if you have none, you can sign a voter affidavit after answering identifying questions.
LA.lineRule: If you are in line at 8:00 PM, you can still vote.

MA.name: Massachusetts

pollHours.note: All polls open by 7:00 AM and close at 8:00 PM; some cities and towns open as early as 5:45 AM. Check your town's hours.

earlyVoting.note: Early voting has ended. Sites and hours varied by city or town.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by your local election office by 5:00 PM on Oct 27, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Postmarked by Nov 3, received by 5:00 PM Nov 6, 2026; in person or in a drop box by 8:00 PM on Election Day
mailBallot.note: Return it to your local election office or a city/town drop box by 8 PM Nov 3. Don't count on handing it in at your polling place; some towns say they cannot accept mail ballots there.

MA.sameDayRegistrationNote: Massachusetts does not offer Election Day registration.
MA.registrationNote: The deadline was Oct 24, 2026 (5 PM in person, 11:59 PM online, or postmarked that day). If you are not registered, you cannot vote in this election.
MA.voterId: Most voters do not need ID; you may be asked for one (such as a driver's license, state ID, or a recent utility bill or other document with your name and address) if you are voting in Massachusetts for the first time, are listed as inactive, or in a few other cases.
MA.lineRule: If you are in the polling place or in line at the door when polls close at 8 PM, you can still vote.
MA.sourceNote: The Secretary of the Commonwealth's site (sec.state.ma.us) blocked every fetch (bot challenge / redirect loop), and the mass.gov flyer returned 403. 2026 dates come from official city/town election pages (Boston, Watertown, Truro); hours, line rule, ID rule and mail receipt deadline come from Massachusetts General Laws ch. 54. The ID summary also matches NBC Boston's 2026 guide, which cites the state site.

MD.name: Maryland

earlyVoting.note: Early voting has ended. Centers were open 7 AM–8 PM daily, including the weekend.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by Oct 27, 2026 to get it by mail; Oct 30 online to print at home; Nov 3 in person at your local board of elections
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Postmarked by Nov 3, received by 10:00 AM Nov 13, 2026; in a drop box or hand-delivered by 8:00 PM on Election Day
mailBallot.note: Use an official ballot drop box or your local board of elections by 8 PM Nov 3. Dropping it in a mailbox on Election Day does not guarantee a same-day postmark.

MD.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can register and vote at your assigned polling place on Election Day by bringing a document that proves where you live, such as an MVA license or ID, paycheck, bank statement, or utility bill.
MD.registrationNote: The advance deadline was Oct 13, 2026. You can still register and vote on Election Day at the polling place for your address with proof of residence.
MD.voterId: Most voters do not need ID; some first-time voters will be asked for one, such as a photo ID or a current utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, or government document showing your name and address.
MD.lineRule: If you are in line at 8 PM, you will be allowed to vote.

ME.name: Maine

pollHours.note: Opening time varies by town: between 6:00 AM and 8:00 AM, or as late as 10:00 AM in towns under 500 people. All polls close at 8:00 PM (towns under 100 people may close once everyone has voted). Ask your town clerk for your opening time.

earlyVoting.note: In-person absentee voting at your town or city clerk's office, no reason needed. Hours vary by town.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by your town clerk by Oct 29, 2026 (unless special circumstances apply)
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by your town or city clerk by 8:00 PM on Election Day (Nov 3, 2026); postmarks do not count
mailBallot.note: You can mail it, hand it to your clerk, or use a local ballot drop box. If your ballot has not arrived, you can go to the polls on Nov 3 to cancel it and vote in person.

ME.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can register in person at your town office or city hall, or at the polls, through the close of polls on Election Day. Bring ID and proof of where you live.
ME.registrationNote: Mail and online registration closed Oct 13, 2026, and registration at the BMV closed Oct 27, 2026. In-person registration stays open through 8:00 PM on Election Day.
ME.voterId: Maine does not require ID to vote; if you are registering for the first time, bring a photo ID, birth certificate, Social Security card, or a document with your name and Maine address such as a utility bill or bank statement.
ME.lineRule: If you are at the polling place when polls close at 8:00 PM, you can still vote.
ME.sourceNote: WebFetch was blocked (403) by maine.gov; the same official pages were read with curl.

MI.name: Michigan

pollHours.note: Local time. Most of Michigan is on Eastern Time; four Upper Peninsula counties on the Wisconsin border use Central Time.

earlyVoting.note: Every community must offer early voting Oct 24 to Nov 1. Some communities chose to start earlier (up to 29 days before the election) or to add Monday, Nov 2. Sites and hours vary; check your city or township clerk at Michigan.gov/Vote.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Online or by mail: received by 5:00 PM Friday, Oct 30, 2026. In person at your clerk's office: by 4:00 PM Monday, Nov 2, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by 8:00 PM on Election Day
mailBallot.note: You can return it to your clerk's drop box or clerk's office by 8:00 PM on Election Day, or bring it to your early voting site through Nov 1. Mailing it this close to the election is not recommended.

MI.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can register in person at your city or township clerk's office through 8:00 PM on Election Day with proof of residency, then vote there with an absentee ballot or at your polling place.
MI.registrationNote: Online and mail registration closed Oct 19, 2026. From Oct 20 through Nov 3, 2026, you can still register in person at your local clerk's office with proof of residency.
MI.voterId: You will be asked for a photo ID such as a Michigan driver's license or state ID (expired is OK), another state's license, a U.S. passport, or a military, student, tribal or government photo ID; if you don't have one, you can sign an affidavit and vote a regular ballot.
MI.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close at 8:00 PM, you can still vote.
MI.sourceNote: The Secretary of State lists only the mandatory early voting dates (Oct 24 to Nov 1, 2026). The optional earlier start and the Monday option are described as rules, not 2026 dates, so they are not used in start/end. Mail request deadlines are stated as 'Friday before Election Day' and 'the day before Election Day'; the 2026 calendar dates were filled in from that rule. The Central Time note for the Upper Peninsula is general knowledge; the official page says only 'local time'.

MN.name: Minnesota

pollHours.note: Some towns with fewer than 500 residents open as late as 10:00 AM. Check your polling place.

earlyVoting.note: In-person absentee voting began Sept 18. New in 2026, Early Voting (you put your ballot in the counter yourself) began Oct 16. Every county has at least one location; hours vary, so check your county election office.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: No firm deadline is listed; the state recommended applying by Oct 20, 2026. It is now too late to count on mail, so vote early in person by Nov 2 or at the polls.
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by Election Day, Nov 3, 2026; if you drop it off yourself, by 5:00 PM on Election Day
mailBallot.note: Postmarks do not count. Drop it off at the office that sent it or a ballot drop box. Do not bring an absentee ballot to your polling place. A witness must sign your ballot envelope.

MN.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can register at your polling place on Election Day with proof of residence, such as a Minnesota driver's license or ID with your current address, or a photo ID plus a recent bill. You can also register when you vote early in person.
MN.registrationNote: Pre-registration closed 20 days before the election (Oct 14, 2026). You can still register when you vote early in person through Nov 2, or at your polling place on Election Day.
MN.voterId: If you are already registered at your current address and name, you do not need ID; if you are registering or updating, bring proof of residence, such as a Minnesota driver's license or ID with your current address.
MN.lineRule: If you are in line by 8:00 PM, you can still vote.
MN.sourceNote: sos.mn.gov blocked direct fetches with a bot-check page. All content came from Internet Archive copies of these official pages, taken Sept 25 to Oct 30, 2026. The Oct 14 pre-registration close date is calculated from the official rule that registration closes 20 days before the election.

MO.name: Missouri

earlyVoting.note: No-excuse in-person absentee voting runs Oct 20 through 5:00 PM Nov 2 at sites set by your local election authority; check your county. You must show photo ID. In-person absentee voting with an approved excuse began Sept 22.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by your local election authority by 5:00 PM on Oct 21, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by your local election authority by 7:00 PM on Election Day
mailBallot.note: You need an approved reason, such as being away on Election Day, illness or disability, or religious belief. Most mailed absentee ballots must be notarized (not required if you are voting absentee due to illness or disability). Postmarks do not count.

MO.sameDayRegistrationNote: Missouri does not offer Election Day registration.
MO.registrationNote: The deadline was Oct 7, 2026. If you are not registered, you cannot vote in this election.
MO.voterId: Bring a photo ID issued by Missouri or the U.S. government, such as a Missouri driver's or nondriver license (OK if it expired after the last general election), U.S. passport, or military or veteran ID; without one you can vote a provisional ballot that counts if you return with ID that day or your signature matches.
MO.lineRule: If you are in line at 7:00 PM, you have the right to vote.
MO.sourceNote: The Secretary of State's 2026 calendar lists only the registration deadline. The 2026 dates for absentee voting (Sept 22 start, Oct 20 no-excuse start, Oct 21 request deadline, Nov 2 end) come from Johnson County's official election calendar, and match the statutory rules described on sos.mo.gov. The mail return deadline is from RSMo 115.293.

MS.name: Mississippi

earlyVoting.note: No early voting for all voters. Voters with an accepted excuse (such as working on Election Day or being out of town) could vote absentee in person at the Circuit or Municipal Clerk's office, Sept 21 until noon Saturday, Oct 31, 2026.

mailBallot.returnDeadline: Postmarked by Nov 3, received by Nov 10, 2026
mailBallot.note: Only some voters can vote absentee by mail: those 65 or older, those with a permanent or temporary disability, and those temporarily living outside their county. Contact your Circuit Clerk to request a ballot. The receipt window is five business days after Election Day.

MS.sameDayRegistrationNote: Mississippi does not offer same-day registration.
MS.registrationNote: The deadline was Oct 5, 2026 (in person, or mail applications postmarked by then). There is no way left to register for the Nov 3 election.
MS.voterId: Bring photo ID, such as a Mississippi driver's license or state ID, U.S. passport, military or tribal photo ID, government employee ID, Mississippi college student ID, or a free Mississippi Voter ID Card; without it you vote an affidavit ballot that counts only if you show ID at the Circuit Clerk's office within five business days.
MS.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close, you can still vote.
MS.sourceNote: The official mail-ballot rule (postmarked by Election Day, received within five business days) comes from the Secretary of State's 2024 absentee guide; Nov 10, 2026 is computed from that rule. The U.S. Supreme Court upheld this window in Watson v. RNC (June 29, 2026). A 2026 law (HB 908) would move the deadline only if federal law were found to preempt it, which the Court did not find. In-person absentee dates come from a WLOX news report. The mail-ballot request deadline and the in-line-at-closing rule were not confirmed on an official page.

MT.name: Montana

pollHours.note: Polling places with fewer than 400 in-person voters may open as late as noon; voters there get a mailed notice. All close at 8:00 PM.

earlyVoting.note: In-person absentee voting at your county election office, no reason needed. By law, ballots are available 30 days before Election Day (Oct 4 fell on a Sunday). Requests are due by noon Nov 2. Hours vary by county; check your county.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by your county election office by noon on Nov 2, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by 8:00 PM on Election Day (Nov 3, 2026); postmarks do not count
mailBallot.note: You can return it by mail, at your county election office, or at any polling place in your county on Election Day.

MT.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can register late and vote at your county election office (or a location it designates) on Election Day until 8:00 PM. A 2025 law (SB 490) that would have ended Election Day registration at noon for federal races was blocked by a court in May 2026.
MT.registrationNote: Regular registration closed Oct 5, 2026. Late registration at your county election office runs through noon Monday, Nov 2, and again on Election Day until 8:00 PM.
MT.voterId: Bring a Montana driver's license or state ID, U.S. passport, military ID, tribal photo ID, Montana concealed carry permit, or a Montana university system or NAIA school photo ID; any other photo ID must be paired with a current bill, bank statement, paycheck, or government document showing your address, and without ID you can vote a provisional ballot.
MT.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close at 8:00 PM, you can still vote.
MT.sourceNote: sosmt.gov blocked all fetches (firewall 403). Used the Montana Code Annotated 2025 (official legislature site) and news reporting. The Oct 5 regular registration deadline is from search results (30 days before the election), not an official page. The SB 490 injunction (May 11, 2026) is from Montana Free Press; I found no later ruling, so confirm late-registration hours with your county. The line rule comes from Montana Free Press reporting of Secretary of State guidance, not an official page.

NC.name: North Carolina

earlyVoting.note: Early voting ends at 3:00 PM on Saturday, Oct 31. You can vote at any early voting site in your county. Sites and hours vary by county; check your county.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by 5:00 PM on Oct 20, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by 7:30 PM on Election Day
mailBallot.note: Include a copy of your photo ID (or an ID Exception Form) with your ballot. You can also hand it in at your county board of elections office, or at an early voting site while it is open.

NC.sameDayRegistrationNote: Only during early voting (Oct 15 to 3:00 PM Oct 31) at an early voting site in your county, with proof of where you live. It is not available on Election Day for most voters.
NC.registrationNote: The regular deadline was 5:00 PM on Oct 9, 2026. Same-day registration at early voting sites ended at 3:00 PM on Saturday, Oct 31, 2026. Registration is now closed for this election.
NC.voterId: Bring a photo ID such as a North Carolina driver's license or DMV ID (unexpired or expired one year or less), a U.S. passport, a free voter ID from your county board, an approved student or government employee ID, or a military, veterans or tribal photo ID; if you have none, you can still vote by filling out an ID Exception Form.
NC.lineRule: If you are in line at your assigned polling place at 7:30 PM, you can still vote.

ND.name: North Dakota

pollHours.note: Varies by county or city: polls open between 7:00 AM and 9:00 AM and close between 7:00 PM and 9:00 PM, local time. North Dakota spans Central and Mountain time zones. Check your hours in the My Voting Information portal.

earlyVoting.note: Varies by county; check your county. Not every county offers early voting. Where offered, it runs on days the county auditor picks within the 15 days before Election Day.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Apply to your county auditor early enough to get the ballot and mail it back before Election Day; no ballots are issued on Election Day except in emergencies
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by the close of polls on Election Day (Nov 3, 2026); postmarks do not count
mailBallot.note: Return by mail, to a county drop box, or in person to the county auditor. Absentee ballots are not accepted at polling places.

ND.sameDayRegistrationNote: North Dakota has no voter registration. Any U.S. citizen 18 or older who has lived in North Dakota for 30 days can vote with a valid North Dakota ID.
ND.registrationNote: North Dakota does not require voter registration, so there is no deadline. Bring valid ID and vote at your polling place on Nov 3 (you must have lived in North Dakota for the 30 days before the election).
ND.voterId: Bring a North Dakota driver's license, North Dakota non-driver ID, tribal ID or tribal letter, or long-term care certificate showing your current address (digital IDs are not accepted); if it is out of date, add a bill, bank statement, paycheck, or government document, or vote a set-aside ballot and show valid ID to the county auditor within 13 days.
ND.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close, you can still vote.
ND.sourceNote: The early voting window (Oct 19 to Nov 2) is worked out from the 15-day rule in N.D. Century Code 16.1-07-15; the state pages give no single 2026 date range because each county sets its own schedule.

NE.name: Nebraska

pollHours.note: Polls are open 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM in the Central Time zone and 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM in the Mountain Time zone (western Nebraska), local time. Both close at the same moment.

earlyVoting.note: In-person early voting is at your county clerk or election commissioner's office.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by 6:00 PM on Oct 23, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by close of polls on Election Day (8:00 PM Central / 7:00 PM Mountain)
mailBallot.note: Ballots postmarked on time but arriving after polls close are not counted. Return it to your county election office or a secure drop box. Include your driver's license or state ID number or a copy of your photo ID.

NE.sameDayRegistrationNote: Nebraska does not offer same-day registration.
NE.registrationNote: Online and mail registration closed Oct 16, 2026, and in-person registration closed at 6:00 PM on Oct 23, 2026. There is no way left to register for the Nov 3 election (except narrow exceptions such as people naturalized after the deadline).
NE.voterId: Bring a photo ID with your name and photo (it can be expired), such as a Nebraska driver's license or state ID, U.S. passport, military or tribal ID, or Nebraska college or government ID; without one you vote a provisional ballot that counts only if you show ID in person at your county election office by Tuesday, Nov 10.
NE.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close, you can still vote.
NE.sourceNote: The in-line rule and the 'show ID by the Tuesday after the election' rule are confirmed from the Secretary of State's May 2026 primary press release; Nov 10 is that rule applied to the general election.

NH.name: New Hampshire

pollHours.note: Hours vary by town or city. By law, polls must open by 11:00 AM and cannot close before 7:00 PM. Many places run 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM; Nashua has used 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM. Check your town clerk.

earlyVoting.note: New Hampshire has no in-person early voting. Voters with a qualifying reason can request an absentee ballot from their town or city clerk.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Request from your town or city clerk by Nov 2, 2026 (the day before the election); a photo ID is required to apply
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by your town or city clerk by 5:00 PM on Nov 3, 2026 if mailed; by 5:00 PM on Nov 2 if delivered in person
mailBallot.note: Allowed reasons include being away on Election Day, disability or illness, religious observance, work or caregiving duties, and a winter storm warning.

NH.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can register at your polling place on Election Day. Bring proof of U.S. citizenship (such as a birth certificate, passport, or naturalization papers), plus proof of age, identity, and where you live.
NH.registrationNote: Registration before the election closes at your town's last supervisors of the checklist session, 6 to 13 days before Nov 3 (dates vary by town). You can still register at your polling place on Election Day with proof of citizenship.
NH.voterId: Bring a photo ID: a driver's license or non-driver ID from any state, a U.S. passport or passport card, or a military ID (expired up to 5 years, or any age if you are 65 or older); student IDs are no longer accepted, and without ID you can vote only if an election official personally knows you.
NH.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close, you can still vote.
NH.sourceNote: sos.nh.gov blocked all fetches (403). Used NH statutes (gc.nh.gov), the City of Dover's 2026 general election page, NHPR, and NCSL instead. The 6:00 AM/8:00 PM range is from search results (Nashua, Green Papers), not an official page. The 6-to-13-day registration window is from Vote411, not an official page. The line rule is from RSA 654:7-a (via Justia) and NHPR reporting of Secretary of State guidance.

NJ.name: New Jersey

earlyVoting.note: Mon–Sat 10 AM–8 PM, Sun 10 AM–6 PM. Vote at any early voting site in your county; no appointment needed.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: By mail: received by Oct 27, 2026. In person at your County Clerk's office: by 3:00 PM on Nov 2, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Postmarked by Nov 3, received by 8:00 PM Nov 9, 2026; in person or drop box by 8:00 PM on Election Day
mailBallot.note: Return it to a county drop box or your county Board of Elections by 8 PM Nov 3. If your signature is missing or doesn't match, the county will send a cure form.

NJ.sameDayRegistrationNote: New Jersey does not offer Election Day registration.
NJ.registrationNote: The deadline was Oct 13, 2026 (21 days before the election). If you are not registered, you cannot vote in this election.
NJ.voterId: Most voters do not need ID; some first-time voters who registered by mail without a verified driver's license or SSN number must show ID (a photo ID or a current document like a utility bill or bank statement with your name and address) or vote a provisional ballot.
NJ.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close at 8 PM, you must be allowed to vote.

NM.name: New Mexico

earlyVoting.note: Early voting began Oct 6 at county clerk offices; more sites opened Oct 17. Early voting ends Saturday, Oct 31. Sites and hours vary by county; check your county clerk.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by Oct 20, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by 7:00 PM on Election Day
mailBallot.note: Postmarks do not count. You can return your ballot to your county clerk's office, a secure drop box, or any Election Day polling location by 7:00 PM Nov 3.

NM.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can register and vote at the same visit during early voting and at any polling location on Election Day. Bring a physical photo ID from a government, tribe, or school (it can be expired); if it does not show your current address, also bring a utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, or government document from the last 90 days.
NM.registrationNote: Online and mail registration closed Oct 6, 2026. You can still register and vote in person on Election Day (and on Oct 31, the last day of early voting).
NM.voterId: Most voters do not need ID; you give your name, year of birth, and address. First-time voters who registered by mail without ID must show a photo ID or a document with their name and address, and same-day registrants need a photo ID.
NM.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close, you can still vote.
NM.sourceNote: The Secretary of State's 2026 dates sheet shows its dates as images that could not be read, so specific dates (Oct 6, Oct 17, Oct 20, Oct 31) come from Santa Fe County's official clerk page.

NV.name: Nevada

pollHours.note: You can vote at any vote center in your county on Election Day.

earlyVoting.note: Hours and sites vary by county; check your county.

mailBallot.returnDeadline: Postmarked by Nov 3, received by 5:00 PM on Nov 7, 2026
mailBallot.note: Active voters were mailed a ballot automatically. You can also drop it off at any early voting site or, on Election Day, any vote center until 7:00 PM.

NV.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can register and vote in person at an early voting site or Election Day vote center. Bring a valid Nevada driver's license, Nevada ID card, DMV interim document, or Nevada tribal ID; if it does not show your current address, also bring proof of residence such as a recent utility bill or bank statement.
NV.registrationNote: Registration by mail or in person closed Oct 6, 2026, and online registration to vote by mail closed Oct 20, 2026. You can still register online or in person through Nov 3 and vote in person.
NV.voterId: Most voters do not need ID; you must show ID only if your sample ballot label says 'ID Required' or you are registering on the same day.
NV.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close at 7:00 PM, you can still vote.
NV.sourceNote: nvsos.gov returned empty pages, so dates come from Clark County's official 2026 General Election guide (state law sets the early voting, registration, and mail deadlines). The line rule comes from secondary sources (news reports), not an official page. A voter ID constitutional amendment (Question 7) is on the 2026 ballot and is not in effect for this election.

NY.name: New York

earlyVoting.note: Early voting has ended. Sites and hours varied by county.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: By mail or online by Oct 24, 2026; in person at your county board of elections by Nov 2, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Postmarked by Nov 3, received by Nov 10, 2026
mailBallot.note: Any voter can use an early mail ballot; an absentee ballot needs a reason. You can also drop off your ballot at any poll site in your county or at your county board of elections before 9:00 PM on Election Day.

NY.sameDayRegistrationNote: New York does not have Election Day registration. The only same-day option was 'Golden Day' on Oct 24, 2026, the first day of early voting, and it has passed.
NY.registrationNote: The deadline was Oct 24, 2026, which was also Golden Day (register and vote the same day). There is no way left to register for the Nov 3 election.
NY.voterId: Most voters do not need to show ID; only first-time voters who did not provide ID when they registered must show a photo ID or a recent utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, or government check, and without it you can still vote an affidavit ballot.
NY.lineRule: If you are in line by 9:00 PM, you can stay in line and vote.
NY.sourceNote: elections.ny.gov (State Board of Elections) blocked both WebFetch and curl with a Cloudflare challenge (403). We used the NY Attorney General's 2026 key-dates page for all dates, NYC's official 311 page for poll hours, ID, and the line rule, and NYC Votes (NYC Campaign Finance Board) for early mail versus absentee eligibility. The NYC pages are written for the city, but these are statewide statutory rules.

OH.name: Ohio

earlyVoting.note: In-person early voting is at your county board of elections (or its early voting center). Ohio sets the same hours statewide; the last day is Sunday, Nov 1 (1:00-5:00 PM). There is no early voting on Monday, Nov 2.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by your county board of elections by 8:30 PM on Oct 27, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by 7:30 PM on Election Day
mailBallot.note: New in 2026: mailed ballots that arrive after 7:30 PM on Election Day are not counted, even if postmarked in time. You can also drop it in your county board's secure drop box; you cannot turn it in at a polling place.

OH.sameDayRegistrationNote: Ohio does not offer same-day registration.
OH.registrationNote: The deadline was Oct 5, 2026. Registration is closed for this election; if you register now, it applies to the next election.
OH.voterId: Bring an unexpired photo ID: Ohio driver's license, state ID or BMV interim ID, U.S. passport or passport card, or U.S. military, Ohio National Guard, or VA ID; without one you can vote a provisional ballot and must show ID at your board of elections within four days.
OH.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close, you can still vote.
OH.sourceNote: The Ohio Secretary of State site (ohiosos.gov) blocked all fetches with a security challenge. Dates and rules come from official county board of elections pages (Franklin and Stark counties). Poll hours and the in-line rule are from R.C. 3501.32 (codes.ohio.gov). The four-day provisional-ID window is from NCSL. The rule that mailed ballots must arrive by 7:30 PM on Election Day comes from Senate Bill 293 (R.C. 3509.05(D)), effective March 20, 2026.

OK.name: Oklahoma

earlyVoting.note: Early voting runs 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM Oct 28-30 and 8:00 AM to 2:00 PM on Saturday, Oct 31. You must vote at an early voting location in the county where you are registered. No excuse is needed.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by 5:00 PM on Monday, Oct 19, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: By mail: received by your County Election Board by 7:00 PM on Election Day, Nov 3, 2026. By hand: delivered by close of business on Monday, Nov 2, 2026
mailBallot.note: A standard absentee ballot affidavit must be notarized; many banks, libraries, and other places notarize it for free. Physically incapacitated voters need two witnesses instead.

OK.sameDayRegistrationNote: Oklahoma does not offer Election Day registration.
OK.registrationNote: The registration deadline for the Nov 3 election was Oct 9, 2026. It is too late to register for this election.
OK.voterId: Bring a photo ID issued by the U.S. government, the State of Oklahoma, or a federally recognized tribe that shows your name and has not expired (or never expires), or the voter ID card your County Election Board mailed you; without ID you can vote a provisional ballot by signing a sworn affidavit.
OK.lineRule: If you are in line by 7:00 PM, you can still vote.
OK.sourceNote: The line rule comes from the State Election Board's August 2026 runoff press release ("All eligible voters in line by 7 p.m. will be permitted to vote"). No November-specific page restating it was found.

OR.name: Oregon

pollHours.note: Oregon votes by mail, so there is no polling place to go to. Drop boxes and county elections offices take ballots until 8:00 PM local time on Election Day (most of Malheur County uses Mountain Time). County office hours vary; 7:00 AM is Multnomah County's Election Day opening time, so check your county.

earlyVoting.note: Oregon has no separate early voting. Every active voter is mailed a ballot about 20 days before the election. You can return it any day at an official drop box or your county elections office, which can also help you vote or replace a lost ballot.

mailBallot.returnDeadline: Postmarked by Nov 3, received by Nov 10, 2026; or dropped off by 8:00 PM on Election Day
mailBallot.note: Ballots were mailed starting Oct 14. If you mail it now, ask the post office to hand-postmark it, or use an official drop box. If your signature is challenged, you have 21 days after the election to fix it.

OR.sameDayRegistrationNote: Oregon does not offer Election Day registration. You had to register 21 days before Election Day.
OR.registrationNote: The registration deadline was Oct 13, 2026 (online by 11:59 PM Pacific). It is too late to register for this election.
OR.voterId: No ID is needed to return your ballot; your signature on the return envelope is checked against your voter registration record.
OR.lineRule: If you are in line at a drop site at 8:00 PM, you can still turn in your ballot.
OR.sourceNote: The state pages do not list Election Day office hours. The 7:00 AM opening time comes from a Multnomah County press release and is only an example. The Mountain Time note for Malheur County is general knowledge and was not confirmed on an election page.

PA.name: Pennsylvania

earlyVoting.note: Pennsylvania has no traditional early voting. Until 5:00 PM on Oct 27, 2026, you could apply for a mail ballot at your county election office, then fill it out and hand it in there the same day. That deadline has passed.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by 5:00 PM on Oct 27, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by your county election office by 8:00 PM on Election Day (postmarks do not count)
mailBallot.note: Return it by mail, at a county drop box, or at your county election office. You must return your own ballot unless you have a disability and named an agent in writing. Sign and date the outer envelope, or your ballot will not be counted.

PA.sameDayRegistrationNote: Pennsylvania does not have same-day registration.
PA.registrationNote: The deadline was Oct 19, 2026. There is no way left to register for the Nov 3 election.
PA.voterId: Most voters do not need to show ID; if you are voting at your polling place for the first time, bring a photo ID (such as a PA driver's license or PennDOT ID, U.S. passport, military, student, or employee ID) or a non-photo ID with your name and address (such as a voter registration card, current utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, or government check).
PA.lineRule: If you are in line by 8:00 PM, you can vote.

RI.name: Rhode Island

pollHours.note: New Shoreham (Block Island) opens at 9:00 AM.

earlyVoting.note: Early voting ends at 4:00 PM on Monday, Nov 2. Locations and hours are set by each city or town; check vote.ri.gov or your local board of canvassers.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Regular applications were due by 4:00 PM Oct 13, 2026; emergency mail ballots are available from your local board of canvassers until 4:00 PM Nov 2
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by 8:00 PM on Election Day (Nov 3, 2026); postmarks do not count
mailBallot.note: You can mail your ballot or use a ballot drop box. Sign the certifying envelope or it will not count.

RI.sameDayRegistrationNote: Rhode Island does not offer same-day registration for this election (Election Day registration applies only to the presidential race in presidential years).
RI.registrationNote: The deadline was Oct 4, 2026 (30 days before the election). No registration option remains for Nov 3.
RI.voterId: Bring a photo ID such as a Rhode Island driver's license or free Rhode Island voter ID card, U.S. passport, school ID, military ID, or government-issued ID or medical card (unexpired or expired less than 6 months); without one you can vote a provisional ballot.
RI.lineRule: If you are in line at 8:00 PM, you can still vote.
RI.sourceNote: vote.sos.ri.gov blocked all fetches (Cloudflare challenge, 403), and the 2026 election calendar PDF is a scanned image that could not be read. Used Rhode Island General Laws (official legislature site), WJAR (turnto10) reporting of the Secretary of State's dates, and search excerpts of the state calendar. The Oct 4 registration deadline comes from search excerpts of the official calendar and matches the 30-day statute. Drop box availability was not confirmed from a page I read in full.

SC.name: South Carolina

earlyVoting.note: Early voting ends at 6:00 PM on Oct 31. Centers are open 8:30 AM to 6:00 PM, Monday to Saturday (closed Sunday, Oct 25). Any registered voter can vote early at any early voting center in their county. Bring your photo ID.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Application received by your county voter registration office by 5:00 PM on Oct 23, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by your county voter registration office by 7:00 PM on Election Day, Nov 3, 2026
mailBallot.note: Valid reasons include being 65 or older, having a disability, or being unable to vote in person because of work or being away. Return it by mail or in person; you must show photo ID to return a ballot in person.

SC.sameDayRegistrationNote: South Carolina does not offer Election Day registration. You must have registered by the October deadline.
SC.registrationNote: In-person registration closed at 5:00 PM on Oct 2, 2026 (unless your county held weekend hours). Online, fax, and email registration closed at 11:59 PM on Oct 4. Mailed forms had to be postmarked by Oct 5.
SC.voterId: Bring a current South Carolina driver's license or DMV ID, an SC voter registration card with photo, a federal military ID, or a U.S. passport; if you could not get a photo ID, bring your non-photo voter registration card and sign a reasonable impediment affidavit to vote a provisional ballot.
SC.lineRule: If you are in line at 7:00 PM, you can still vote.

SD.name: South Dakota

pollHours.note: Local time. South Dakota spans two time zones: eastern counties use Central Time and western counties use Mountain Time.

earlyVoting.note: In-person absentee voting at your county auditor's office, through 5:00 PM on Nov 2 (or the end of office hours, if later). Bring a photo ID or sign an ID affidavit.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Apply to your county auditor; in person until 5:00 PM Nov 2, 2026. Allow time for mailing.
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by your county election official on Election Day in time to reach your precinct before polls close at 7:00 PM
mailBallot.note: A voter who is sick or disabled can get and return a ballot through an authorized messenger; that request must be received by 3:00 PM on Election Day.

SD.sameDayRegistrationNote: South Dakota does not offer same-day registration.
SD.registrationNote: The deadline was Oct 19, 2026. No registration option remains for Nov 3. New for 2026 (SB 175): new registrants who do not provide proof of citizenship are registered as federal-only voters.
SD.voterId: Bring a South Dakota driver's license or non-driver ID, U.S. passport or federal photo ID, tribal photo ID, or a South Dakota school or college photo ID; if you have none, you can sign an affidavit with your name and address and vote a regular ballot.
SD.lineRule: If you are at the polling place, inside or outside, before polls close, you can still vote.
SD.sourceNote: The Secretary of State's absentee page does not list required excuses; any registered voter can apply, so this is shown as 'any voter'. The application must include a copy of photo ID or be notarized.

TN.name: Tennessee

pollHours.note: Opening time varies by county (7:00, 8:00, or 9:00 AM local). All polls close at the same moment: 8:00 PM Eastern / 7:00 PM Central. Check your county's opening time on GoVoteTN.gov.

earlyVoting.note: Early voting has ended. Sites and hours varied by county.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by your county election commission by Oct 24, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by your county election commission by the close of polls on Election Day
mailBallot.note: You need an approved reason, such as being 60 or older, being out of your county during early voting and all of Election Day, or illness or disability. You must return it by mail or carrier (USPS, FedEx, UPS); hand delivery is not allowed.

TN.sameDayRegistrationNote: Tennessee does not offer Election Day registration.
TN.registrationNote: The deadline was Oct 5, 2026. If you are not registered, you cannot vote in this election.
TN.voterId: Bring a photo ID issued by Tennessee or the federal government, such as a Tennessee driver's license, passport, or military ID (expired is OK); college student IDs, out-of-state licenses, and local-government IDs are not accepted.
TN.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close, you will be allowed to vote.
TN.sourceNote: The line rule is quoted from the Secretary of State's Aug 6, 2026 election press release; it is a standing rule, not specific to that election.

TX.name: Texas

pollHours.note: Local time. Most of Texas is on Central time; El Paso and Hudspeth counties are on Mountain time.

earlyVoting.note: Early voting has ended. You could vote at any early voting location in your county.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received (not postmarked) by Oct 23, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by 7:00 PM on Election Day, or postmarked by 7:00 PM on Nov 3 and received by 5:00 PM on Nov 4, 2026
mailBallot.note: You can vote by mail only if you are 65 or older, sick or disabled, out of the county for early voting and Election Day, expected to give birth within three weeks of Election Day, or confined in jail but otherwise eligible.

TX.sameDayRegistrationNote: Texas does not have same-day registration.
TX.registrationNote: The deadline was Oct 5, 2026. There is no way left to register for the Nov 3 election.
TX.voterId: Bring a Texas driver's license, Texas Election Identification Certificate, Texas personal ID card, Texas handgun license, U.S. military ID with photo, U.S. citizenship certificate with photo, or U.S. passport (expired no more than 4 years, or any length of time if you are 70 or older); if you do not have one and cannot reasonably get one, bring a document like a utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, or voter registration certificate and sign a Reasonable Impediment Declaration.
TX.lineRule: If you are inside or waiting to enter your polling place at 7:00 PM, you can still vote.
TX.sourceNote: The line rule comes from the text of Texas Election Code 41.032(a) ("inside or waiting to enter the polling place at 7 p.m.") as shown in search results from texas.public.law. The official statute site would not render, and the Secretary of State's poll-worker PDF (7-30f) could not be parsed. The Central/Mountain time note comes from general knowledge, not a page we read.

UT.name: Utah

pollHours.note: Election Day voting is at county vote centers.

earlyVoting.note: Varies by county; check your county. Early voting began about two weeks before Election Day; most counties end on Friday, Oct 30 (Salt Lake County also has Saturday, Oct 31, 10 AM to 2 PM at the Government Center).

mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by 8:00 PM on Election Day
mailBallot.note: Utah no longer counts mailed ballots that arrive after Election Day, even if postmarked on time. Use a county drop box or a vote center by 8:00 PM on Nov 3 instead of mailing late.

UT.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can register at an Election Day vote center and vote a provisional ballot. Bring one ID proving who you are and one proving where you live.
UT.registrationNote: The deadline to register and get a ballot by mail was Oct 23, 2026. You can still register and vote a provisional ballot in person at a vote center on Election Day.
UT.voterId: Bring one valid photo ID with your name (such as a Utah driver license, state ID, U.S. passport, or military ID; tribal ID need not have a photo), or two documents that together show your name and current address.
UT.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close, you can still vote.
UT.sourceNote: Most of vote.utah.gov was blocked (Cloudflare error) except the voter ID page, so dates come from official county clerk pages (Salt Lake, Cache, Millard). Registration deadline: Cache County lists Oct 23; Millard County's notice says 'Friday, October 22' (Oct 22, 2026 is a Thursday), so Oct 23 is used. The statewide end of early voting and the line rule were not confirmed on an official page.

VA.name: Virginia

earlyVoting.note: Ended 5:00 PM Saturday, Oct 31, 2026, at your local registrar's office or satellite sites. No early voting on Nov 2.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by your local registrar by 5:00 PM on Oct 23, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Postmarked by Nov 3, received by noon Nov 6, 2026; in person or at a drop-off location by 7:00 PM on Election Day
mailBallot.note: You can return your ballot to your registrar's office or a local drop-off location by 7 PM Nov 3. Emergency absentee voting in person is available until 2 PM Nov 2 only for certain late emergencies.

VA.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can register at your polling place on Election Day and vote a provisional ballot, which counts once your registration is approved.
VA.registrationNote: The regular deadline was Oct 23, 2026 (5 PM in person, 11:59 PM online). After that, you can still register and vote a provisional ballot in person at your polling place on Election Day.
VA.voterId: Show an acceptable ID such as a Virginia driver's license (expired is OK), passport, or student ID; if you have none, you can sign an ID Confirmation Statement and still vote a regular ballot.
VA.lineRule: If you are in line at 7:00 PM, you will be allowed to vote.

VT.name: Vermont

pollHours.note: Each town sets its opening time between 5:00 AM and 10:00 AM. All polls close at 7:00 PM. Ask your town clerk for your opening time.

earlyVoting.note: Vote early in person at your town or city clerk's office during business hours, starting 45 days before the election or as soon as ballots arrive, through the clerk's last office hours before Election Day. Hours vary by town.

mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by your town clerk before the office closes on Nov 2, 2026, or brought to your polling place by 7:00 PM on Election Day
mailBallot.note: Ballots are mailed automatically to all active registered voters; you can also use a drop box in your town or bring the ballot to the polls. If you need a ballot, request one from your town clerk by 5:00 PM (or office closing) on Nov 2. Your clerk will contact you if your ballot needs a fix.

VT.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can register at your town clerk's office during business hours, or at your polling place on Election Day, and vote the same day.
VT.registrationNote: Vermont has no registration deadline. You can register any day up to and including Election Day, Nov 3, 2026.
VT.voterId: Most voters do not need ID; if you are a first-time voter who registered by mail or online and your ID number could not be verified, bring a photo ID such as a driver's license or passport, or a current utility bill, bank statement, or government document.
VT.lineRule: If you are at the polling place when polls close at 7:00 PM, you can still vote.
VT.sourceNote: The Sept 19 early voting start is 45 days before Election Day, per the Secretary of State's rule; actual start depended on when each town received ballots.

WA.name: Washington

pollHours.note: Washington votes by mail; there are no traditional polling places. County voting centers are open during business hours (opening time varies by county; 8:00 AM is typical but not set by state law) and close at 8:00 PM on Election Day. Drop boxes close at 8:00 PM.

earlyVoting.note: All voters get a ballot by mail. You can also vote in person at a county voting center from Oct 16 through Election Day (until 8 PM on Nov 3). Hours vary by county; check your county.

mailBallot.returnDeadline: In a drop box or voting center by 8:00 PM on Election Day, or postmarked by Nov 3 and received by Nov 23, 2026
mailBallot.note: No stamp needed. The state advises mailing more than a week before Election Day, so this close to the election a drop box or voting center is safest; if you mail it, ask a postal clerk to postmark it.

WA.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can register or update your registration in person at a county voting center or elections office until 8 PM on Election Day and vote then.
WA.registrationNote: The online and mail deadline was Oct 26, 2026. You can still register in person at a voting center or county elections office until 8 PM on Nov 3.
WA.voterId: No ID is needed to vote by mail; your signature is checked. At a voting center, show a photo ID (driver's license, state ID, student, tribal, or employer ID) or sign a declaration; without ID you vote a provisional ballot counted if your signature matches.
WA.lineRule: If you are inside or in line at a voting center at 8:00 PM, you must be allowed to vote. Drop boxes close at 8:00 PM sharp.
WA.sourceNote: The Nov 23 receipt date is derived from state law (RCW 29A.60.190: postmarked ballots received by the day before county certification) and the state's Nov 24 certification date. The line rule and voting-center ID rule come from RCW 29A.40.160.

WI.name: Wisconsin

earlyVoting.note: In-person absentee voting at your municipal clerk's office. Days and hours vary by city, village, or town, and some offices offer only limited hours; check MyVote or your clerk.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by your municipal clerk by 5:00 PM on Oct 29, 2026 (photo ID copy required with request)
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by your municipal clerk by 8:00 PM on Election Day, Nov 3, 2026
mailBallot.note: Return by mail or deliver it to your municipal clerk. Postmarks do not count; a ballot that arrives after 8:00 PM on Nov 3 is not counted.

WI.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can register at your polling place on Election Day, Nov 3, 2026, from 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM. Bring a proof of residence document.
WI.registrationNote: Online and mail registration closed Oct 14, 2026. In-person registration at your municipal clerk's office closed at 5:00 PM on Oct 30, 2026. You can still register at your polling place on Election Day with proof of residence.
WI.voterId: Bring a Wisconsin driver's license or state ID card, U.S. passport, military ID, tribal ID, veterans ID, naturalization certificate issued within 2 years, or a qualifying Wisconsin college or university ID; an expired license, state ID, military ID, or passport works only if it expired after the Nov 5, 2024 general election.
WI.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close at 8:00 PM, you can still vote.
WI.sourceNote: elections.wi.gov and myvote.wi.gov returned 403 to direct fetches. Deadlines came from the Internet Archive copy of the official MyVote Voter Deadlines page (snapshot Oct 23, 2026). Poll hours, the line rule, and photo ID rules came from the Wisconsin Statutes (6.78 and 5.02(6m)) on docs.legis.wisconsin.gov.

WV.name: West Virginia

earlyVoting.note: Early voting ends Saturday, Oct 31 at 5:00 PM. Held at the county courthouse, an annex, or a designated community location.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Received by your county clerk by Oct 28, 2026
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Postmarked by Nov 3, received by Nov 9, 2026 (hand-deliver to the county clerk by Nov 2)
mailBallot.note: Excuses include illness or disability, travel, school, or work away from your county. Ballots cannot be returned at polling places; one person may hand-deliver no more than two voters' ballots.

WV.sameDayRegistrationNote: West Virginia does not offer same-day registration.
WV.registrationNote: The deadline was Oct 13, 2026. No registration option remains for Nov 3.
WV.voterId: Bring a valid, unexpired photo ID, such as a West Virginia or other state driver's license or ID, U.S. passport, military ID, or a photo student ID from a West Virginia school; without one you can vote a provisional ballot, and county clerks issue free voter ID cards.
WV.lineRule: If you are in line when polls close at 7:30 PM, you will get a waiting-voter permit and can still vote.
WV.sourceNote: Poll hours, line rule, and absentee excuse list come from the West Virginia Code (official legislature site) because the Secretary of State pages fetched did not state them.

WY.name: Wyoming

earlyVoting.note: In-person absentee voting at your county clerk's office, no reason needed. Not available on Election Day.

mailBallot.requestDeadline: Request from your county clerk any day before Election Day (by Nov 2, 2026); allow up to 7 days for mail delivery
mailBallot.returnDeadline: Received by your county clerk's office by 7:00 PM on Election Day (Nov 3, 2026)
mailBallot.note: Return by mail or in person to your county clerk's office. Mail-in absentee voters do not need to show ID.

WY.sameDayRegistrationNote: You can register and vote at your polling place on Election Day. Bring a Wyoming driver's license or other ID, plus proof of U.S. citizenship and Wyoming residency (a 2025 law requires both; a Wyoming license without a non-citizen marking counts as proof of citizenship).
WY.registrationNote: Regular registration closed Oct 19, 2026. You can still register in person at your county clerk's office and vote absentee through Nov 2, or register and vote at your polling place on Nov 3.
WY.voterId: Bring an ID: a Wyoming or other-state driver's license or ID card, tribal ID, U.S. passport, military ID, a University of Wyoming, Wyoming community college, or Wyoming public school student ID, a Medicare or Medicaid card, or a Wyoming concealed firearm permit; free state IDs are available at Driver Services.
WY.lineRule: If you are in line at 7:00 PM, you can still vote.
WY.sourceNote: Poll hours come from NCSL, and the line rule comes from a reproduction of W.S. 22-13-117 (via search), because no Secretary of State page I read stated them. NCSL says a voter without ID gets a provisional ballot and must show ID to the county clerk by the next business day; the Secretary of State page did not say this.
